For **`add-dark-mode-toggle`**: close it with a recorded rationale — don't delete it, and don't try to "complete" it.

- **Why not complete:** the team already decided not to pursue dark mode this quarter (blocked on design finalizing the color palette), so racing to fill in placeholders would ship something explicitly deprioritized.
- **Why not delete:** deleting erases the reasoning trail. Since this could resurface once the palette is finalized, a closed packet with the rationale attached ("not pursued this quarter — blocked on design palette; team decision from meeting") saves whoever picks it back up from re-litigating the same discussion or wondering why it stalled. Nothing was merged, so closing carries no risk of losing shipped work.
- **Why not just ignore it:** leaving it as `scaffold` keeps showing as noise in the status report — closing it moves it to an honest terminal state so it stops flagging.

One flag on the other packet: **`refactor-auth-flow`** shouldn't go through this workflow at all — it's `invalid` only because the missing file hasn't landed yet, but a teammate is actively working on it. This skill is explicitly not for in-progress packets, so the right move there is just to leave it alone (or let your teammate know it's tripping the status check) rather than closing/deleting/completing it yourself.
